title: Dijkstra et al 2014, Managing the health of the elite athlete: a new integrated performance health management and coaching model, BJSM 48(7):523-531
why: The only published model naming who leads health, who leads coaching, who they both report to, and which decisions each may not take. Source of the coach-cannot-overrule-medical rule.

title: Interassociation Consensus: Independent Medical Care for College Student-Athletes Best Practices, NCAA Sport Science Institute
why: Ten guiding principles plus the unchallengeable autonomous authority wording. The only setting where the reporting line is legislated.

title: AASP Certified Mental Performance Consultant candidate handbook, Dec 2021
why: States in the certifying body own words that CMPC is not sport psychologist and that psychological services are governed by licensing boards. The psych boundary.

title: AASP, What is a Certified Mental Performance Consultant?
why: The public-facing scope list: what a CMPC is trained to help with. No clinical claim anywhere on it.

title: Reardon et al 2019, Mental health in elite athletes: IOC consensus statement, BJSM 53(11):667-699
why: IOC position that mental health is inseparable from physical health and raises injury risk. Abstract only; the body is paywalled.

title: Thomas, Erdman, Burke 2016, Nutrition and Athletic Performance, joint position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, Dietitians of Canada and ACSM, MSSE 48(3):543-568
why: Names the referral target (registered dietitian/nutritionist) and the CSSD credential. The nutrition boundary.

title: Drew et al 2023, Health Systems in High-Performance Sport: Key Functions to Protect Health and Optimize Performance in Elite Athletes, Sports Med 53(8):1479-1489
why: Frames the support team as a health system with stewardship and a fifth sport-specific function. Abstract only.

title: USADA, How can athlete support help with anti-doping responsibilities?
why: Carries the WADA Code definition of Athlete Support Personnel. Evidence that ASP is a rule-book category, not a discipline.

title: Reid, Stewart, Thorne 2004, Multidisciplinary sport science teams in elite sport: comprehensive servicing or conflict and confusion?, The Sport Psychologist 18(2):204-217
why: The founding paper on role conflict in athlete support teams. Publisher returned 403; cited by title and claim only.

title: Burns and Collins 2023, Interdisciplinary practice in performance sport: a scoping review of evidence of collaboration, Eur J Sport Sci 23(9):1877-1891
why: The state of the evidence: 22 included articles, four themes, terminology used interchangeably.

title: Performance support team effectiveness in elite sport: a narrative review, 2024
why: Sought for failure modes. Publisher returned 403 on two attempts; not used for any claim.
